summary: Reviewed the World Cup SEO optimisation spec against the current page implementation and repository conventions in the pack. The biggest architectural risks are SSOT drift for operational claims, ambiguous ownership between the parent live-sport page and the World Cup child page, and copy promises that are not clearly backed by the fixture component contract. Overall the spec is directionally sound, but it needs a few contract-level clarifications before implementation.
appears_sound: The spec keeps the page at `/live-sport/world-cup`, which fits the existing App Router location shown in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx` and avoids dated URL churn.

The spec preserves the existing resilient fixture fetch pattern rather than moving API calls into a client component; the current page fetches matches server-side and renders `WorldCup2026Fixtures` with `matches={matches}` in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:75` and `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:223`.

Moving the fixtures table directly after the hero matches the existing component boundary: `WorldCup2026Fixtures` is already isolated as a feature component in `components/features/world-cup/WorldCup2026Fixtures.tsx`.

Adding BreadcrumbList JSON-LD is architecturally consistent with the current page's server-rendered JSON-LD approach via `jsonLdSafeStringify` in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:7` and `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:120`.

findings.description: The spec leaves the current booking-rule claim of no deposits untouched, but project conventions say groups of 10+ require a £10 per-person deposit. This creates a contract mismatch between the marketing page and the booking policy users encounter downstream.
findings.evidence: Current copy says `No deposits and no minimum spend` in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:145`, while `CLAUDE.md` states `Group deposit: Groups of 10+ on any day, any booking type — £10 per person`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The venue might intentionally waive group deposits for World Cup bookings, but that exception is not stated in the SSOT or spec.
findings.what_would_confirm: Check `docs/SSOT.md` or ask whether World Cup bookings have a documented deposit exception for groups of 10+.

findings.description: The keyword ownership boundary is internally inconsistent: the spec lists `football pub near me` and `pub showing football near me` as primary targets, then says not to target `football pub near me` because the parent `/live-sport` page owns it. That ambiguity can cause the child page to compete with the parent page rather than supporting it.
findings.evidence: The spec's primary targets include `football pub near me`, but the `DO NOT target` section says `football pub near me` belongs to the parent `/live-sport` page.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The primary list may be intended as broader search context rather than explicit on-page targeting.
findings.what_would_confirm: Revise the spec to explicitly assign generic football/live-sport terms to `/live-sport` and World Cup-specific/local terms to `/live-sport/world-cup`.

findings.description: The reorder removes the current intro section containing the page-level `PageTitle`, while another part of the spec says `World Cup Pub Near Heathrow` stays in the H1. The spec needs to state where the H1 lives after the intro section is removed, otherwise implementation may leave the page with the wrong heading contract.
findings.evidence: The current H1-like page title is rendered by `PageTitle` in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:102`, but the new order starts after the hero with a fixtures section header instead.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: `HeroWrapper` may render its `title` as the actual H1, but that component contract is not included in the pack.
findings.what_would_confirm: Verify `HeroWrapper` heading semantics or specify that `PageTitle` remains as the H1 while only the keyword-stuffed paragraphs are removed.

findings.description: The FAQ addition says users should check the fixtures list for selected knockout matches with extended hours until midnight, but the spec does not describe any data or component contract change that would let the fixtures table represent those exceptions. This risks copy promising per-match extended-hour status while `WorldCup2026Fixtures` only receives raw `matches`.
findings.evidence: The current page passes only `matches={matches}` to `WorldCup2026Fixtures` in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:223`, while the spec adds copy about selected knockout hours being visible in the fixtures list.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: `WorldCup2026Fixtures` may already encode selected knockout extended-hour rules internally, but that file's contents are not in the pack.
findings.what_would_confirm: Inspect `components/features/world-cup/WorldCup2026Fixtures.tsx` or specify an explicit extended-hours data source/prop in the spec.

findings.description: The spec continues updating opening hours as static page copy rather than tying hours display to the repo's SSOT/hours utility pattern. Operational hours are a shared data boundary in this project, so manual text updates can drift from management-app hours and SSOT content.
findings.evidence: The current page hardcodes core hours in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:135`, while `CLAUDE.md` says to use `lib/hours-utils.ts` for hours display logic and to treat `docs/SSOT.md` as canonical for operational facts.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: A short static summary may be acceptable for this SEO page if verified against SSOT at implementation time.
findings.what_would_confirm: Confirm whether this page is allowed to carry static event-hours copy, or require the implementation to derive displayed hours from the existing constants/API utilities.

findings.description: The local-area rewrite includes `up to [X] cars`, but the current page already uses `PARKING.capacity` as the shared constant for parking capacity. Leaving this as a placeholder creates an avoidable drift risk or a literal placeholder escaping into customer-facing copy.
findings.evidence: The current implementation renders parking capacity from `PARKING.capacity` in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:294` and `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:360`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The placeholder may simply be shorthand for using the existing constant during implementation.
findings.what_would_confirm: Update the spec to require `PARKING.capacity` rather than a hardcoded number or placeholder.

findings.description: The proposed intro says the schedule is `Updated live from FIFA`, but the current page uses 24-hour ISR and a catch-and-continue fallback. The data freshness and source contract should be precise so page copy does not overpromise live updates.
findings.evidence: The current page sets `revalidate = 60 * 60 * 24` in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:51` and catches fixture fetch failures in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx:75`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The phrase may mean the fixture source is online rather than real-time, and `lib/world-cup-2026` may indeed use FIFA data.
findings.what_would_confirm: Verify the fixture source in `lib/world-cup-2026` and either replace `Updated live` with `Updated regularly` or reduce revalidation if real-time freshness is required.

empty_categories: No client/server boundary violation is introduced by the spec; the fixtures fetch remains server-side in the current architecture.
No new database, raw SQL, or direct management API access is proposed by the spec.
No circular dependency risk is visible from the pack because the planned changes stay within the page, schema rendering, and existing feature component boundary.
No shared mutable state issue is visible in the planned page reorder.
